parsed.rationale: All five participating records are type-alias-objects with empty `fields_or_signature` lists, meaning the structural pipeline matched them solely on shape (zero-field type aliases) rather than on shared semantic content. The aliases carry unrelated domain names — `Discogs.Release.Label`, `Discogs.Release.ReleaseArtist`, `Discogs.Master.ReleaseArtist` in the `Artwork` package versus `Release` and `Artist` in the `Metadata` package — and live in files with distinct responsibilities (`DiscogsArtworkService.swift` vs. `_Plant_ReleaseRepository.swift` / `_Plant_ArtistRepository.swift`). The `shared_field_count: 2` with `jaccard: null` and `differing_slots: null` further confirms the match is structural coincidence (both sides happen to be empty-body type aliases) rather than duplicated logic. Consolidating these aliases would conflate Discogs API response modelling with the Metadata domain model, introducing an inappropriate cross-package coupling.
